claim_boundary.supports: For Gaussian-integer sector amplitudes a, b, both nonzero, the phase-blind weights (|a|^2, |b|^2) do not determine the unnormalized Hadamard readout (|a+b|^2, |a-b|^2) (kernel-checked for every such pair, not only for the (1,1)/(1,-1) witnesses); mixing always doubles the total weight; the readout difference is 4 Re(a conj b); a zero first sector (a = 0, by w_eq_zero the fiber of weight 0 is the single point 0) or a zero second sector forces the readout to depend on the other weight only, so it descends (descends_when_zero_sector, descends_when_second_zero). Exact fiber and readout tables for ten weight pairs, including the unrealizable weight 3 (for which descends=true is vacuous: both fibers empty).
claim_boundary.does_not_support: Complex-Hilbert amplitudes beyond Z[i]; normalized or projective states; more than two sectors; mixes other than the unnormalized 2x2 Hadamard; the embedding of Z[i] into C (non-descent on the Gaussian-lattice fibers gives non-descent on the full complex phase fibers only after that embedding is formalised); the identification of the module readout with the source declarations phaseBlind/mix/readout over Vec GaussInt Bool (H008/H010), which is a modelling identification, not a checked one; any measurement, branch or physical interpretation of the phase fiber.
claim_boundary.narrowest_claim: Over Z[i] with the unnormalized two-sector Hadamard readout: both sector amplitudes nonzero implies the weight pair does not determine the readout; a zero first or zero second sector implies it does.
claim_boundary.next_test: Decide non-descent of the normalized projective readout w(a+b)/(2(w(a)+w(b))) for n>=3 complex sectors under a unitary mix other than the 2x2 Hadamard, by exhibiting a fiber pair with different readouts or a descending fiber.

second_review.notes: Cold read of run 20261021T132245Z_staged. I recompiled lean4/PhaseBlindFiber.lean (Lean 4.35.0; ten anchors, axioms only propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound, witness_readouts axiom-free; only unused-tactic linter warnings). The p1 construction copies of the Lean, Python and Rust files are byte-identical to the production files and to the source_pins; the checker sha equals the p2 checker pin. Anchor fidelity: no_descent is a genuine non-existence statement (not exists f, forall x y, w x = w a -> w y = w b -> readout x y = f (w x, w y)) for ALL nonzero Gaussian a, b, proved through fiber_changes_readout (one of the rotations i*b or -b changes the readout, via cross^2 + Im^2 = w a * w b), so the claim 'kernel-checked for every such pair, not only for the (1,1)/(1,-1) witnesses' is true. readout_total and readout_interference are general ring identities. descends_when_zero_sector and descends_when_second_zero are existence statements with f = (p.2,p.2) / (p.1,p.1) and say what the text says. witness_readouts is labelled an instance. Earlier-pass amendments: ALL applied. (a) second-slot zero: descends_when_second_zero exists and is anchored, case (5,0) is native, semantic mutant second_sector_zero_treated_as_generic exists and is rejected (G3_WITNESS:distinct_readouts); (b) w_eq_zero is in anchors and p2_checks.lean; (c) does_not_support now names the Z[i] -> C embedding, the H008/H010 modelling identification and the vacuity of descends=true on the unrealizable pair (3,3); (d) unit_orbit_as_fiber now carries the true readouts of the orbit instead of only changing fiber_sizes. narrowest_claim now says 'a zero first or zero second sector'. No hard-coded value in the checker (cases come from the public input via E.bound; fibers by box enumeration, readouts by W +- 2c, flags recomputed); no weakening visible: every leaf is type-checked with is_int/bool, readouts compared as sorted lists, 268 coordinate mutants and 7 semantic mutants all rejected, order-reversal control accepted. Residual weaknesses (none forces a rebuild). (1) The zero-sector descent theorems are stated with the literal point x = 0 (resp. y = 0) and a free other variable; no anchor ties 'weight of the first sector is 0' to 'x = 0' inside a single descent statement (w_eq_zero is a separate lemma), and they do not have the fiber-quantified shape of no_descent. The prose 'by w_eq_zero the fiber of weight 0 is the single point 0' is a one-line composition left to the reader. (2) mixing_preserves_total is still a flipped boolean (total_doubled=False with readouts left intact); it is caught only because the checker recomputes the flag. (3) The checker's consistency assertion 'positive realizable weights must not descend' is enforced only on the ten public cases; generality rests entirely on the Lean theorem. (4) The source witnesses over Vec GaussInt Bool are never touched (correctly disclaimed). next_test (normalized projective readout, n>=3, non-Hadamard unitary) is the node's own unpaid obligation and is not equal to does_not_support. DAG: PROVED_LEAN on the source rests on two fixed witnesses; the new result proves a general Z[i] two-sector statement but does not touch the source Vec GaussInt Bool declarations, so the statement should be narrowed (status not raised).

dag_suggestion.statement: Over Z[i] with the unnormalized two-sector Hadamard readout (|a+b|^2, |a-b|^2): for any nonzero Gaussian amplitudes a, b no function of the phase-blind weights (|a|^2, |b|^2) determines the readout on the product of the weight fibers (rotation by i or by -1 suffices); mixing doubles the total weight and the readout difference is 4 Re(a conj b); a zero first or zero second sector makes the readout descend. The source witnesses (1,1)/(1,-1) are instances. Complex Hilbert amplitudes, normalized or projective states, more than two sectors, other mixes and the link to the Vec GaussInt Bool declarations (H008/H010) are not covered.
dag_suggestion.bottleneck: Z[i] -> C embedding and the identification with the source H008/H010 declarations are not formalised; normalized/projective readout with n>=3 sectors and non-Hadamard unitary mixes are open.

earlier_pass.notes: I recompiled lean4/PhaseBlindFiber.lean (Lean 4.35.0, exit 0; all eight anchors report only propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound, witness_readouts none) and the p1 construction copies of the Lean, Python and Rust sources are byte-identical to the production files. The load-bearing anchors say what supports claims: no_descent is a genuine non-existence statement (not exists f, forall x y, w x = w a -> w y = w b -> readout x y = f (w x, w y)) for every nonzero Gaussian a, b, and it is proved through the unit rotations i and -1 (fiber_changes_readout), so the non-descent really is through unit-phase orbits as the source's 'unit phases' import requires. readout_total and readout_interference are general identities. WEAKNESSES. (1) descends_when_zero_sector only treats the FIRST sector at weight 0 and the fixed x = 0 (statement: exists f, forall y, w y = w b -> readout 0 y = f (0, w y)); it never quantifies over x with w x = 0, and 'a zero-weight sector has a trivial fiber' is not the conclusion of any anchor (w_eq_zero, which gives triviality, is a lemma that is not in the anchor list). The second-slot zero case (b = 0, e.g. weights (5,0)) is neither proved in the kernel nor present in the nine native cases (only (0,5) and (0,0)). So the profile sentences 'a zero-weight sector ... descends' and narrowest_claim 'one zero sector implies it does' are stronger than the kernel statement: it is 'first sector zero'. By symmetry the second-slot case is a one-line proof, but it is not paid. (2) The certificate flag descends is len(readouts) <= 1, which is vacuously true for the unrealizable pair (3,3) (empty fibers, record realizable=false, descends=true). The checker only forces not-descends when realizable and both weights positive, so it is consistent, but descends=true on an empty fiber must not be read as 'readout descends'. (3) The weight fiber here is the Gaussian-lattice fiber, a subset of the full complex phase fiber; non-descent on a subset implies non-descent on the larger fiber when the amplitudes are embedded in C, but that Z[i] -> C bridge is not formalised anywhere (no Complex in the module); the module also does not touch the source declarations phaseBlind/mix/readout over Vec GaussInt Bool, so the match between the module's readout (|a+b|^2,|a-b|^2) and the source's mix is a modelling identification, not a checked one. does_not_support covers 'beyond Z[i]' but does not name the Z[i] -> C embedding or the source-declaration identification. CHECKER. check_candidate.py is genuinely independent: it brute-forces the fiber over an integer box (producer solves for y at each x with isqrt), recomputes the readout via W +- 2c with c = Re(a conj b) (producer adds Gaussian integers), compares readouts as sorted lists, every leaf (fiber_sizes, realizable, readouts, distinct_readouts, total_doubled, descends) is compared with exact type checks, and coverage equals the public cases. No tolerance, no order-insensitivity that hides a defect (order is canonical sorted). Limited to nine weight pairs, so the generality rests wholly on the Lean. MUTANTS. real_sign_fiber_only and equal_weights_imply_equal_readout are genuine near misses to the stated bridge; zero_sector_treated_as_generic is a genuine boundary near miss; unit_orbit_as_fiber changes only fiber_sizes and leaves the readouts of the full fiber, so it is closer to a flipped field than a counterexample (and its rationale says the readouts differ, which the mutant does not model); unrealizable_weight_accepted and mixing_preserves_total are flipped flags (the latter flips a boolean while keeping the data that proves it false). Missing near misses: (a) second-slot zero weight (5,0) read as non-descending or as untested; (b) sign-convention near miss using Re(a b) instead of Re(a conj b) in the readout difference (a rotation-by-i swap that makes the readout look invariant under multiplication of b by i); (c) a normalised/projective readout presented as the same result. next_test is this node's own unpaid obligation (normalised projective, n>=3, non-Hadamard mix) and is not equal to does_not_support (it is a specific instance of two of its clauses). DAG: the node is already PROVED_LEAN with source statement 'interference does not descend through the phase-blind quotient'; the result establishes it only for the Z[i], two-sector, unnormalised Hadamard model, so the statement should be narrowed, not the status raised.
